tagline: Simple screen and camera recording for polished async videos.
verdictSummary: A recorder with a trim step and a hosted share page — capture screen and webcam together, trim to the useful part, publish to a clean URL — is a real weekend build on browser recording APIs and ffmpeg. What doesn't come with it is Tella's actual polish: beautiful preset layouts, templates, and team sharing.
coreLoopDIY: A browser-based recorder that captures screen and webcam together, a simple trim step, and a one-click publish to a hosted share page.
whatYouLose: browser extension and native app polish
whyPeopleStillPay: People want a video that looks good without editing or deployment chores — they pay for that finish and convenience, not because capturing a screen recording is hard.
notes: A more attainable target than Loom in this catalogue: a good 'yes, but you lose the polish' entry.
prompt:
Build a browser-based screen recorder: capture screen and webcam together (webcam as a small circular overlay), recorded directly in the browser. After recording, add a simple trim step — set in and out points on a basic timeline, preview, then render the final video with ffmpeg. Publish with one click: upload the rendered video to your own server, which serves it at a clean, unlisted URL with a simple player, a title, and your name — nothing else on the page. Extract a poster frame for link previews, and track a basic view count. Keep the original recording and the rendered output organized by date and title.

Do not build layout templates, zoom or pan effects, or a team library — this is a recorder with a trim step, not an editor, and that's a deliberate, honest scope limit.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Tella recordings?
faq.a: Yes, if you've downloaded them — Tella lets you export your videos, and those work as source files here. Share pages, view counts, and any team library history stay in Tella.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: Watching a shared recording works fine on a phone browser. Recording itself relies on desktop screen-capture APIs, so this is a desktop tool for creating videos.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting and storage for your own videos, typically a few dollars a month at personal volume, growing with how much you keep.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: The polish. Tella's preset layouts and templates make a recording look considered with zero effort; here, what you record is what you get, trimmed but not styled.
